name: OPA132 / OPA2132 / OPA4132
tagline: The original CMoy chip: an 8 MHz, 20 V/µs Burr-Brown FET-input part that runs well on 9 V with the soft 'BB sound'.

lineage.note: Datasheet origin January 1995 (PDS-1309B Dec 1995). Chu Moy's original CMoy op-amp; parent of the OPA134.
Renumbered SBOS054: A 2004, B 2015, C 2024 (new-fab die, trim pins NC). PDIP parts obsolete; SOIC active.

part_numbers.note: PDIP-8 standard grade; pins 1/8 Offset Trim through SBOS054B. 'New' DIP stock is suspect.
SOIC-8 standard grade; /2K5 reel. Current lots are new-fab die, pins 1/8 NC.
PDIP-8 high (DC) grade; tangentsoft says the grade matters only for DC specs.
SOIC-8 high grade. OPA132U/2K5G4 variant reported only by a radiolocman index.
PDIP-8 dual; tangentsoft's CMoy beginner pick (~$5.40 early 2000s). LCSC C201554. No trim pins.
SOIC-8 dual; also OPA2132UA/2K5, OPA2132UAE4 (Farnell 1206934; E4 = lead finish). Jameco 904448.
High-grade dual, PDIP-8/SOIC-8; reportedly active. TI OPA2132U pages live.
PDIP-14 quad; genuine but obsolete, so new DIP-14 parts are old stock or fakes.
SOIC-14 quad; also /2K5, /2K5E4, UAE4. Jameco 905491; Farnell 1212302, Newark 80K6028.

key_specs.condition: tangentsoft: 8.3 V min for 2 V/330 Ω

key_specs.value: Trim on pins 1/8 to SBOS054B; NC from SBOS054C
key_specs.condition: single only; dual/quad never had trim

reputation.summary: Chu Moy's original CMoy op-amp and the default in countless CMoy builds. Tangentsoft recommends the OPA2132PA to beginners over the cheaper OPA2134PA: it needs little voltage and rarely oscillates. Its notes (translated on Soomal) call it natural and sweet with few flaws, but not exciting; identical to the OPA134 and about 5% behind the OPA627/637.
typical_uses: CMoy and other 9 V pocket headphone amps
Entry-level op-amp rolling in DACs, CD players, sound cards
Portable audio: clean output from 5.5 V (tangentsoft)
caveats: SBOS054C (Aug 2024) parts are a new-fab die; OPA132 pins 1/8 are NC, so offset-null pots do nothing.
DIP OPA132P/PA and OPA4132PA are obsolete; 'OPA132 discontinued' claims mean the DIP. SOIC versions remain active.
OPA134/OPA2134PA may distort or oscillate in circuits built for the 132, especially at low supply (tangentsoft).
Folklore (Russian DIY notes): OPA2132 drives low impedances better than OPA2134. Fakes reportedly common; buy from authorized distributors.
Soomal's article translates tangentsoft rather than reviewing independently. No ASR or Samuel Groner measurement exists.

counterfeit_notes: No OPA132-specific fake guide exists; fakes are reportedly common, as with OPA2134. Sibling OPA2134/OPA2604 fakes are relabelled TL072-class dies with wipe-off marks or ground tops. New-date DIP singles or quads are suspect. Trim response is no test for SBOS054C lots.
alternatives: AD823 (better bass and detail, less current)

part_numbers_affected: OPA132P / OPA132PA (only if new-fab PDIP lots shipped before obsolescence; unconfirmed)
silicon_changes.identification: SBOS054C or later shows pins 1/8 NC; an offset pot has no effect. Burr-Brown-logo and SBOS054B-era lots are the old die. No marking, PCN or date-code cutover is public.
silicon_changes.summary: TI moved the OPA132 to a new fab and design; an E2E engineer says trim 'has been eliminated in the new FAB change and design' for all packages 'due to improved process'. OPA130, OPA131, OPA134 and molded OPA627 got the same change; TO-99 OPA627, OPA604 and TL071 keep trim.

spec_deltas.parameter: Other electrical specs (Vos, noise, SR, THD, Iq, ESD)
spec_deltas.after: not retrieved; compare the SBOS054B and SBOS054C tables

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Undocumented. A different die from the Burr-Brown silicon behind the reputation; DC-coupled designs lose pins-1/8 offset nulling.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: pin-compatible (TI: no redesign needed), but offset nulling is lost and other spec deltas unknown
silicon_changes.verification: E2E quote (thread 1517005, c. 2025) and diyAudio sibling-part list confirmed. No PCN number; PCNs reportedly went to direct customers.

silicon_changes.identification: No functional tell: the dual and quad never had trim pins. A post-2024 TI date code is the only likely indicator (unconfirmed).
silicon_changes.summary: SBOS054C covers all three parts, and TI calls the OPA132 change a 'new FAB change and design'. No source says whether the dual and quad dies also moved, so this is unconfirmed.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown. If it applies, current OPA2132PA stock (the CMoy favourite) is not the silicon behind its reputation.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: no pin-function change documented for dual or quad; the change itself is unconfirmed
silicon_changes.verification: Searches for OPA2132/OPA4132 PCNs or TI fab statements found nothing; kept at low confidence.

revision_history.changes: Initial release of OPA132/OPA2132/OPA4132; the single has Offset Trim on pins 1 and 8. No copy found.
PDS-1309B; Japanese edition PDSJ-1309B in the LEBRA archive. Changes not shown. TI later renumbered it SBOS054.
Model dated 02/23/96, REV. A 7/20/96. OPA134 model 'adapted from OPA132 model 9/24/96'.
Change list not retrieved; old Burr-Brown-style layout.
Converted to TI 'OPAx132' format; cited by TI PSpice OPA132.LIB (Final 1.2, 05FEB2019). Last revision with Offset Trim.
'Changed OPA132 pin 1 and pin 8 from Offset Trim to NC'; existing layouts need no redesign. New-fab die; no PCN found.

revision_chains.note: Later letters (1996–2000) unknown. PDSJ-1309B at Nihon University; alldatasheet 82130 probably the US copy.
Old-layout mirrors may be original/A. Rev-specific seeds inferred. An OPA1644 datasheet miscites SBOA054 as SBOS054.

refuted_claims: OPA4132PA (DIP-14) was a genuine orderable: TI lists it PDIP (N) 14-pin as OBSOLETE.
TI did not cite 'a more precisely trimmed die'; E2E says 'eliminated in the new FAB change and design', 'removed due to improved process'.
'OPA132 has been discontinued' is only partly true: PDIP OPA132P/PA are obsolete, SOIC OPA132U/UA active.
corrections: Statuses: OPA132P/PA obsolete; OPA132U/UA active; OPA4132PA obsolete; OPA4132UA active; OPA2132 family reportedly active. Combined OPA132P/U entry split.
silicon_changes split: OPA132 new-fab/trim-NC change at high confidence; possible dual/quad fab move at low confidence.
SBOS054C 'January 1995 - Revised August 2024' and its Rev C pin note confirmed.
SBOS054A 'Revised June 2004' and SBOS054B 'Revised September 2015' confirmed.
OPA130, OPA131, OPA134 and molded OPA627 trim → NC confirmed; TO-99 OPA627 keeps trim.
Noise condition corrected to 8 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz; I_B headline is 5 pA typ.
Original CMoy op-amp confirmed as the OPA132, parent of the audio-specific OPA134.
Radiolocman OPA132 URL is indexed in its encoded form as listed.
Mirrors seen in results raised to medium confidence; TI product pages raised to high.
Added mirrors (Jameco 904448, ic114, datasheetspdf 1427995, datasheet4u 475548, radiolocman) plus OPA2132 product, part-details and store pages and LCSC C201554.
Layouts: UT Austin, octopart 111710, westfloridacomponents are old layout (original or A); fevaris and studylib are TI format (B or C).
